opening.text: A handshake can mean a lot. Two people agree, shake hands, and both know what they've promised. In some places, a handshake is stronger than a signed paper. A covenant is like that. It's a promise between us and God. He keeps His part. We choose to keep ours.

mainMessage.text: A covenant is a sacred promise between God and us. When we keep it, we are never alone.

blocks.text: **A promise we prepare for** God doesn't ask us to rush into covenants. He invites us to understand them and then to make them with open eyes.

Now I say unto you, if this be the desire of your hearts, what have you against being baptized in the name of the Lord, as a witness before him that ye have entered into a covenant with him, that ye will serve him and keep his commandments, that he may pour out his Spirit more abundantly upon you?
Elder Dale G. Renlund of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Accessing God’s Power through Covenants” from the April 2023 general conference.
A covenant is a pledge that we should prepare for, clearly understand, and absolutely honor.
Good promises are made with care.
**The other hand is steady** In a covenant, there are two hands. One of them never lets go. That one is His.
Know therefore that the Lord thy God, he is God, the faithful God, which keepeth covenant and mercy with them that love him and keep his commandments to a thousand generations;
Elder Gerrit W. Gong of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Covenant Belonging” from the October 2019 general conference.
Our God is a God of covenant.
He keeps His word.
**Walking side by side** A covenant puts us next to the Savior. The Lord invites us to take His yoke and learn from Him.

Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.
Elder David A. Bednar of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “With the Power of God in Great Glory” from the October 2021 general conference.
We take the Savior’s yoke upon us as we learn about, worthily receive, and honor sacred covenants and ordinances.
We don't carry the load alone.
**What He promises** The Lord says He is bound when we do what He says. That is a remarkable thing to hear from God.
I, the Lord, am bound when ye do what I say; but when ye do not what I say, ye have no promise.
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Overcome the World and Find Rest” from the October 2022 general conference.
Those who live the higher laws of Jesus Christ have access to His higher power.
His promises answer our effort.
**When we slip** We all fall short sometimes. The memory of what we promised can call us back.
For the mountains shall depart, and the hills be removed; but my kindness shall not depart from thee, neither shall the covenant of my peace be removed, saith the Lord that hath mercy on thee.
Elder Dale G. Renlund of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Accessing God’s Power through Covenants” from the April 2023 general conference.
When we falter, the memory of our covenants with God helps us return to the path.
His kindness stays, even when we stumble.
**Put it first** King Benjamin's people wanted to make a covenant to do God's will. They chose it with all their hearts.

And we are willing to enter into a covenant with our God to do his will, and to be obedient to his commandments in all things that he shall command us, all the remainder of our days, that we may not bring upon ourselves a never-ending torment, as has been spoken by the angel, that we may not drink out of the cup of the wrath of God.
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Overcome the World and Find Rest” from the October 2022 general conference.
Cherish and honor your covenants above all other commitments.
Keep your first promise first.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they kept a promise to God, even when it was hard. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: The rainbow

blocks.text: After the flood, God made a promise to Noah and to the earth. He gave a sign so people would remember.

I do set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant between me and the earth. And it shall come to pass, when I bring a cloud over the earth, that the bow shall be seen in the cloud: And I will remember my covenant, which is between me and you and every living creature of all flesh; and the waters shall no more become a flood to destroy all flesh.
God gave a sign to help us remember. He still keeps that promise.

application.text: First, think of one covenant you have made. Second, ask yourself how you are keeping it. Third, choose one small way to honor it better this week.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that God keeps His promises. I know covenants bring me closer to Him. I know that Jesus Christ walks beside me when I keep them. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to think of one covenant you have made.
I invite you to ask yourself how you are keeping it.
I invite you to choose one small way to honor it better this week.
blessings: You will feel closer to God.
Your faithfulness will bring you joy.

closingVerse.text: If ye love me, keep my commandments.

opening.text: A ship in a storm drops its anchor. The wind pushes. The waves roll. But the anchor holds, and the ship stays put. A covenant works the same way. When life gets rough, our promises to God hold us fast.

mainMessage.text: A covenant is an anchor. It connects us to God and keeps us steady when everything else shakes.

blocks.text: **Forging the anchor** An anchor is made carefully. A covenant should be made with preparation and understanding.

Now I say unto you, if this be the desire of your hearts, what have you against being baptized in the name of the Lord, as a witness before him that ye have entered into a covenant with him, that ye will serve him and keep his commandments, that he may pour out his Spirit more abundantly upon you?
Elder Dale G. Renlund of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Accessing God’s Power through Covenants” from the April 2023 general conference.
A covenant is a pledge that we should prepare for, clearly understand, and absolutely honor.
Take time to make it right.
**The chain is God's** The chain is strong because He holds the other end. He is faithful to those who love Him.
Know therefore that the Lord thy God, he is God, the faithful God, which keepeth covenant and mercy with them that love him and keep his commandments to a thousand generations;
Elder Gerrit W. Gong of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Covenant Belonging” from the October 2019 general conference.
Our God is a God of covenant.
The other end is secure.
**Joined to the Savior** The anchor is set in Him. We are joined to Jesus Christ, and He carries our weight.

Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.
Elder David A. Bednar of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “With the Power of God in Great Glory” from the October 2021 general conference.
We take the Savior’s yoke upon us as we learn about, worthily receive, and honor sacred covenants and ordinances.
He holds us in the storm.
**Holding in the wind** The Lord says He is bound when we do what He says. We hold, and He holds.
I, the Lord, am bound when ye do what I say; but when ye do not what I say, ye have no promise.
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Overcome the World and Find Rest” from the October 2022 general conference.
Those who live the higher laws of Jesus Christ have access to His higher power.
We hold to Him, and He holds to us.
**Re-setting the anchor** Sometimes an anchor drags. We slip. The covenant lets us set it again.
For the mountains shall depart, and the hills be removed; but my kindness shall not depart from thee, neither shall the covenant of my peace be removed, saith the Lord that hath mercy on thee.
Elder Dale G. Renlund of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Accessing God’s Power through Covenants” from the April 2023 general conference.
When we falter, the memory of our covenants with God helps us return to the path.
A slip is not the end.
**Fixed for life** King Benjamin's people covenanted to keep God's will for the rest of their days. That is a settled life.

And we are willing to enter into a covenant with our God to do his will, and to be obedient to his commandments in all things that he shall command us, all the remainder of our days, that we may not bring upon ourselves a never-ending torment, as has been spoken by the angel, that we may not drink out of the cup of the wrath of God.
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Overcome the World and Find Rest” from the October 2022 general conference.
Cherish and honor your covenants above all other commitments.
Let your promise to God be your anchor.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when a promise to God kept them steady. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: The young soldiers who kept their word

blocks.text: A group of young men had been taught to keep the commandments. They were true at all times.

And they were all young men, and they were exceedingly valiant for courage, and also for strength and activity; but behold, this was not all—they were men who were true at all times in whatsoever thing they were entrusted. Yea, they were men of truth and soberness, for they had been taught to keep the commandments of God and to walk uprightly before him.
Their steadiness came from being taught and from choosing. A covenant gives us that same kind of steadiness.

application.text: First, think about a time you felt unsteady. Second, ask what promise to God could steady you. Third, renew that promise in prayer.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that my covenants hold me fast. I know God never lets go. I know Jesus Christ is my anchor. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to think about a time you felt unsteady.
I invite you to ask what promise to God could steady you.
I invite you to renew that promise in prayer.
blessings: You will find an anchor for your soul.
You will feel the Lord's steadiness.
You will feel peace as you renew your promise.

closingVerse.text: Which hope we have as an anchor of the soul, both sure and steadfast, and which entereth into that within the veil;

opening.text: A lamp can sit on a table all day. It has a bulb, a shade and a switch. But until it is plugged in, it gives no light. The power was always there in the wall. The lamp just wasn't connected. Covenants are like the plug. They connect us to the power of God.

mainMessage.text: Covenants connect us to God's power. When we keep them, His strength flows into our lives.

blocks.text: **Know what you are plugging into** A wise person checks before plugging in. We prepare for covenants and learn what they mean.

Now I say unto you, if this be the desire of your hearts, what have you against being baptized in the name of the Lord, as a witness before him that ye have entered into a covenant with him, that ye will serve him and keep his commandments, that he may pour out his Spirit more abundantly upon you?
Elder Dale G. Renlund of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Accessing God’s Power through Covenants” from the April 2023 general conference.
A covenant is a pledge that we should prepare for, clearly understand, and absolutely honor.
Understand it, then commit.
**The source never runs out** The power in the wall doesn't wear out. God is faithful, and He keeps covenant for thousands of generations.
Know therefore that the Lord thy God, he is God, the faithful God, which keepeth covenant and mercy with them that love him and keep his commandments to a thousand generations;
Elder Gerrit W. Gong of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Covenant Belonging” from the October 2019 general conference.
Our God is a God of covenant.
The source is always on.
**The connection** The cord has to reach the wall. We are connected to the Savior when we take His yoke and keep our promises.

Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.
Elder David A. Bednar of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “With the Power of God in Great Glory” from the October 2021 general conference.
We take the Savior’s yoke upon us as we learn about, worthily receive, and honor sacred covenants and ordinances.
Stay connected to Him.
**Power flows both ways** When we do our part, the Lord does His. He says He is bound when we do what He says.
I, the Lord, am bound when ye do what I say; but when ye do not what I say, ye have no promise.
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Overcome the World and Find Rest” from the October 2022 general conference.
Those who live the higher laws of Jesus Christ have access to His higher power.
Keep your end of the cord in place.
**Plug back in** Sometimes the cord comes loose. We can plug in again. His kindness and His covenant do not leave us.
For the mountains shall depart, and the hills be removed; but my kindness shall not depart from thee, neither shall the covenant of my peace be removed, saith the Lord that hath mercy on thee.
Elder Dale G. Renlund of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Accessing God’s Power through Covenants” from the April 2023 general conference.
When we falter, the memory of our covenants with God helps us return to the path.
Reconnect and the light comes back.
**Don't unplug for something small** We wouldn't unplug the lamp to plug in a toy. King Benjamin's people chose to keep the covenant for the rest of their lives.

And we are willing to enter into a covenant with our God to do his will, and to be obedient to his commandments in all things that he shall command us, all the remainder of our days, that we may not bring upon ourselves a never-ending torment, as has been spoken by the angel, that we may not drink out of the cup of the wrath of God.
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Overcome the World and Find Rest” from the October 2022 general conference.
Cherish and honor your covenants above all other commitments.
Guard the connection.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when keeping a covenant gave them strength they didn't expect. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego

blocks.text: Three young men were told to bow to a golden image or be thrown into a furnace. They would not.

If it be so, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace, and he will deliver us out of thine hand, O king. But if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up.
They said "but if not." They would stay faithful whether or not they were rescued. That is what it looks like to honor a covenant.

If ye keep my commandments, ye shall abide in my love; even as I have kept my Father's commandments, and abide in his love.
These things have I spoken unto you, that my joy might remain in you, and that your joy might be full.

opening.text: Two climbers on a mountain are tied together by a rope. If one slips, the other holds. Neither plans to fall, but both trust the rope. A covenant is like that rope. It ties us to the Savior. When we slip, He is the one who holds.

mainMessage.text: Covenants tie us to the Savior. When we hold up our end, He holds us.

blocks.text: **Tying in with care** Climbers check their knots before they climb. We prepare before we make a covenant.

Now I say unto you, if this be the desire of your hearts, what have you against being baptized in the name of the Lord, as a witness before him that ye have entered into a covenant with him, that ye will serve him and keep his commandments, that he may pour out his Spirit more abundantly upon you?
Elder Dale G. Renlund of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Accessing God’s Power through Covenants” from the April 2023 general conference.
A covenant is a pledge that we should prepare for, clearly understand, and absolutely honor.
Check the knot, then climb.
**The partner who never lets go** One climber can trust the other. We can trust God. He keeps covenant and shows mercy.
Know therefore that the Lord thy God, he is God, the faithful God, which keepeth covenant and mercy with them that love him and keep his commandments to a thousand generations;
Elder Gerrit W. Gong of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Covenant Belonging” from the October 2019 general conference.
Our God is a God of covenant.
He is a reliable partner.
**Roped to the Savior** We are roped to Jesus Christ. When we take His yoke, we share the climb with Him.

Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.
Elder David A. Bednar of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “With the Power of God in Great Glory” from the October 2021 general conference.
We take the Savior’s yoke upon us as we learn about, worthily receive, and honor sacred covenants and ordinances.
You climb with Him, not alone.
**Both hands on the rope** The rope works when both climbers do their part. The Lord says He is bound when we do what He says.
I, the Lord, am bound when ye do what I say; but when ye do not what I say, ye have no promise.
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Overcome the World and Find Rest” from the October 2022 general conference.
Those who live the higher laws of Jesus Christ have access to His higher power.
Do your part, and He does His.
**When the foot slips** Every climber slips sometime. The rope keeps us from falling all the way. The memory of the covenant pulls us back.
For the mountains shall depart, and the hills be removed; but my kindness shall not depart from thee, neither shall the covenant of my peace be removed, saith the Lord that hath mercy on thee.
Elder Dale G. Renlund of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Accessing God’s Power through Covenants” from the April 2023 general conference.
When we falter, the memory of our covenants with God helps us return to the path.
The rope catches us.
**Climb all the way up** A climber doesn't untie halfway up. King Benjamin's people promised to keep God's will for all the days of their lives.

And we are willing to enter into a covenant with our God to do his will, and to be obedient to his commandments in all things that he shall command us, all the remainder of our days, that we may not bring upon ourselves a never-ending torment, as has been spoken by the angel, that we may not drink out of the cup of the wrath of God.
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Overcome the World and Find Rest” from the October 2022 general conference.
Cherish and honor your covenants above all other commitments.
Stay tied in to the top.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when a friend stayed loyal to them, or when they stayed loyal to a friend. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Jonathan and David

blocks.text: Jonathan and David made a covenant of friendship. It cost Jonathan something.

Then Jonathan and David made a covenant, because he loved him as his own soul. And Jonathan stripped himself of the robe that was upon him, and gave it to David, and his garments, even to his sword, and to his bow, and to his girdle.
A covenant is a promise of love and loyalty. Jonathan gave up what he had to show it. Covenants with God ask for that same loyal love.

application.text: First, think of someone who relies on you to keep your word. Second, ask yourself how you can be more dependable. Third, do one thing today that shows it.

I invite you to ask yourself how you can be more dependable.

opening.text: You buckle a seatbelt before you drive. You don't plan to crash. You buckle it because you love the people in the car, and because you know the road can be unpredictable. Covenants are like that. We make them hoping never to need rescue. But they protect us on the road we can't see.

mainMessage.text: Covenants are a loving protection. We keep them because we love God and trust Him on the road ahead.

blocks.text: **Buckle up on purpose** You don't buckle by accident. We make covenants on purpose, with understanding.

Now I say unto you, if this be the desire of your hearts, what have you against being baptized in the name of the Lord, as a witness before him that ye have entered into a covenant with him, that ye will serve him and keep his commandments, that he may pour out his Spirit more abundantly upon you?
Elder Dale G. Renlund of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Accessing God’s Power through Covenants” from the April 2023 general conference.
A covenant is a pledge that we should prepare for, clearly understand, and absolutely honor.
Make it on purpose.
**The safety was built by someone who cares** A seatbelt exists because someone cared. Covenants exist because God cares. He is faithful to those who love Him.
Know therefore that the Lord thy God, he is God, the faithful God, which keepeth covenant and mercy with them that love him and keep his commandments to a thousand generations;
Elder Gerrit W. Gong of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Covenant Belonging” from the October 2019 general conference.
Our God is a God of covenant.
He designed it with love.
**Held close** A seatbelt holds us close to the seat. A covenant holds us close to the Savior, who invites us to rest in Him.

Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.
Elder David A. Bednar of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “With the Power of God in Great Glory” from the October 2021 general conference.
We take the Savior’s yoke upon us as we learn about, worthily receive, and honor sacred covenants and ordinances.
Stay close to Him.
**It only works when it is on** A seatbelt only helps if it's fastened. The Lord's promise answers our effort.
I, the Lord, am bound when ye do what I say; but when ye do not what I say, ye have no promise.
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Overcome the World and Find Rest” from the October 2022 general conference.
Those who live the higher laws of Jesus Christ have access to His higher power.
Fasten it every day.
**After a bump** A bump on the road jolts us. The memory of our promise to God steadies us again.
For the mountains shall depart, and the hills be removed; but my kindness shall not depart from thee, neither shall the covenant of my peace be removed, saith the Lord that hath mercy on thee.
Elder Dale G. Renlund of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Accessing God’s Power through Covenants” from the April 2023 general conference.
When we falter, the memory of our covenants with God helps us return to the path.
The covenant brings us back to the road.
**For the whole trip** You wear the seatbelt from start to finish. King Benjamin's people promised to keep their covenant for the rest of their days.

And we are willing to enter into a covenant with our God to do his will, and to be obedient to his commandments in all things that he shall command us, all the remainder of our days, that we may not bring upon ourselves a never-ending torment, as has been spoken by the angel, that we may not drink out of the cup of the wrath of God.
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Overcome the World and Find Rest” from the October 2022 general conference.
Cherish and honor your covenants above all other commitments.
Keep it on from start to finish.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they made a promise to God while facing something unknown. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Jacob's promise at Bethel

blocks.text: Jacob was leaving home with nothing. He made a promise to God.

And Jacob vowed a vow, saying, If God will be with me, and will keep me in this way that I go, and will give me bread to eat, and raiment to put on, So that I come again to my father’s house in peace; then shall the Lord be my God:
Jacob made his promise at the start of an uncertain road. God was with him the whole way. That is what covenants offer us too.

application.text: First, think of the road you are on right now. Second, ask what promise to God would help you on it. Third, say a short prayer to renew that promise.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I am grateful for covenants. I know they are a gift from a loving God. I know Jesus Christ protects those who keep them. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to think of the road you are on right now.
I invite you to ask what promise to God would help you on it.
I invite you to say a short prayer to renew that promise.
blessings: You will feel protected and guided.
You will feel His help each day.

closingVerse.text: The Lord will perfect that which concerneth me: thy mercy, O Lord, endureth for ever: forsake not the works of thine own hands.
